title: Automated compilation of Urdu poetry handwritten image datasets for optical character recognition
author: Ijaz, Namoun, et al.

steps.title: Split PDF into page images
steps.instruction: Use Python PDF libraries to convert each page of the scanned Urdu poetry PDF into an individual image file.

steps.title: Segment pages into line images
steps.instruction: Apply OpenCV with the Neighborhood Connected Component Analysis (NCCA) algorithm to each page image to obtain separate line‑level images.

substeps.instruction: Load the page image with OpenCV.
Run an eight‑way Connected Component Labeling (CCL) to label all components.
Calculate the average component height and width.
Ignore components that are significantly smaller or larger than the averages during preprocessing.
Split large components that could cause line merging.
Define each component’s neighbourhood using the average height and width to group components on the same line.
After initial line formation, reconsider previously ignored small components in post‑processing and assign them to the appropriate lines.

steps.title: Manually trim and clean line images
steps.instruction: Inspect each segmented line image and manually remove noise, markings, or extraneous text to ensure a clean line image.

steps.title: Save line images with systematic names
steps.instruction: Store every cleaned line image as a separate PNG file named with its source page and line number (e.g., page_1_line_1.png); note that line numbers may be non‑contiguous because some segments contain no text.

steps.title: Generate text labels via OCR and web lookup
steps.instruction: Obtain Unicode text labels for each line image by running OCR and selecting the best matching reference from an online Urdu text bank.

substeps.instruction: Run the UTRNET Urdu OCR model (CNN‑RNN hybrid) on each line image to produce a predicted transcription.
Scrape the online Unicode text bank for the two poets (Mirza Ghalib and Allama Iqbal) to collect candidate reference texts.
For each candidate reference, compute the Character Error Rate (CER) = (substitutions + deletions + insertions) / total reference characters.
Select the reference text with the lowest CER as the label for the image.

steps.title: Manually verify and correct annotations
steps.instruction: Review each OCR‑derived label, correct any errors, and ensure the text accurately reflects the content of the image.

steps.title: Save annotations to CSV file
steps.instruction: Create an annotations.csv file where column 1 contains the image file name and column 2 contains the verified Unicode text for that image.

steps.title: Compile final dataset and report metrics
steps.instruction: Collect all 2 888 line images (from Mirza Ghalib and Allama Iqbal) with their annotations; report that the UTRNET model achieved a Character Error Rate of 11.13 % and a Word Error Rate of 46.22 % on this dataset without fine‑tuning.
